summary: A privately owned replica of a British Columbia light on Oregon's Cape Perpetua, built in 1976 and closed to the public.

light.note: LighthouseFriends gives a range of 16 miles, about 14 nautical miles.

access.note: Grounds, tower and house are closed to the public; the light can be seen from a pullout on U.S. 101 at milepost 166.

visit.note: Not open to the public; view from the highway only.

facts.agency: Private owner. James A. Gibbs until his death in 2010; the Lighthouse Directory says his family then owned the house and that the property sold in June 2017; no source names the later owner or the buyer.

events.note: Built by James A. Gibbs as a replica of Fiddle Reef Light (Oak Bay, British Columbia)
The Lighthouse Directory gives 1976 as the year of the light
The light is made an official navigational aid
Builder James A. Gibbs dies at his home in Yachats (30 April per Salish Sea Lighthouses; May per LighthouseFriends)
The Lighthouse Directory lists the light as inactive since 2016
Property sold in June 2017 for $489,900 (Lighthouse Directory only; LighthouseFriends says it stayed in the Gibbs family)
Property placed on the market again in 2023 at $2.25 million (LighthouseFriends calls it the first time; the Lighthouse Directory says it was listed in 2016)

notes_for_editor: Thin station: no keepers (the USLHS roster lists none), no official-report coverage (the light dates from 1976, after the corpus and Chronicling America), and no newspaper search was run. Disagreements now stated in the story: (1) tower height: CoastView and LighthouseFriends say 34 ft (10 m); the Lighthouse Directory says 35 ft (11 m); the 11 m record value comes from OSM/Wikidata; (2) Gibbs's death month: Salish Sea Lighthouses gives 30 April 2010; LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory give May 2010; (3) sale history: the Directory says listed 2016, sold June 2017 for $489,900, back on the market 2023 at $2.25 million; LighthouseFriends says the property stayed in the Gibbs family and was first put on the market in 2023 at $2.25 million; (4) official status: LighthouseFriends says made an official navigational aid in 1979; the Directory says the Coast Guard accepted it as a privately maintained aid and the headland never had an official lighthouse. Distance to Yachats: CoastView says 2 miles (3.2 km); LighthouseFriends says 1.8 miles; the story says 'about two miles'. Cook dates: LighthouseFriends and CoastView give landfall or first land sighting on 6 March 1778 and first sighting of the cape on 7 March; the story gives 7 March for the cape and 6 March for land. The Salish biography gives Gibbs's Tillamook Rock service as 'for a year from 1945. to 1948.' (internally inconsistent); the story says only 'in the 1940s'. Wikipedia (lead: family meant to keep it as an official aid, and the Wikipedia death citation) is not used as a source. The Directory names the owners after Gibbs's death (his daughter and her husband); the story says only 'his family' and names no one. The buyer of 2017 is not named by any source. The LighthouseFriends 'Solander Island' optic line is taken as written (LighthouseFriends places Solander Island off the west coast of Vancouver Island; the Directory calls the lens 'acrylic'); the story says only 'optic'.
